belt_speed_variation.control_point_clock: elapsed time from start of observation (after reseating for stability trials)
belt_speed_variation.interpretation: Uniform random speed targets joined by smooth cosine transitions; forces arise from MuJoCo contact friction, not direct body kicks.

belt_stop_observation.braking: half-cosine belt surface speed to zero; no body velocity reset; speed variation and roughness disabled
belt_stop_observation.interpretation: Separate stationary observation; transport pose frequencies and stability rankings are unchanged. Contact planes extend beyond the virtual exit.
belt_stop_observation.rest_criterion: existing 0.5 s contact/orientation window with full XYZ position range <= 1 mm and filtered speed <= 1 mm/s
belt_stop_observation.trigger: after transport measurement at the virtual exit; drop trials only

collision_quality.note: Part volumes are summed; overlapping convex parts are not unioned.

contact_response.interpretation: Solver contact parameters, not a directly specified restitution coefficient. Uncalibrated material response.

active_window.clock: elapsed observation time; includes release for drops, starts after reseating for stability trials
active_window.cutoff: only full physics steps within the window; no restart on recontact; active force pulses end with window_end

surface_roughness.contact_sampling: uniform random geometrically touching loaded contact on belt or wall at impulse time

instantaneous_impulse.energy_policy: External impulse changes generalized velocity through point Jacobian and mass matrix; normal contact dynamics follow
instantaneous_impulse.timing: exponential waits; at most one complete impulse per integration step; contactless events skipped; times rounded up to a step boundary

surface_roughness.interpretation: Uncalibrated complete point impulse J = mass * free velocity change. No finite force duration or shortening at later contact loss. Geometry and inertia determine rotation; no pose forced.
